title: Node inputs: widgets, optional, hidden, force_input

questions.q: An API client sends the string "false" to a BOOLEAN input. What does the node get?
questions.why: validate_inputs calls bool(val), and any non-empty string is true. We ran it.

questions.q: An optional input has default 3 in the schema and is left out of the prompt. What does the function receive?
options: No argument: its Python default applies
questions.answer: No argument: its Python default applies
questions.why: get_input_data passes only what the prompt holds. The schema default is for the editor.

questions.q: A FLOAT input has min 0 and max 1. The prompt sends "nan". What happens?
options: It passes and the node gets NaN
questions.answer: It passes and the node gets NaN
questions.why: float('nan') converts fine, and every comparison with NaN is false, so neither range check fires.

questions.q: What does force_input do on the server?
options: Converts the value to a wire
questions.why: It tells the editor to draw a socket. A constant in the prompt passed in our run.

questions.q: What is a side effect of asking for the hidden input UNIQUE_ID?
options: The node runs on every queue
The node id joins its cache key, so identical copies stop sharing a result
The node is hidden from the menu
The output is written to the PNG
questions.answer: The node id joins its cache key, so identical copies stop sharing a result
